difficultyReason: Two simple categorical facts with one direct deduction. No conditional complexity or multi-step inference required.
stimulus: All mammals are vertebrates. Dogs are mammals.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All vertebrates are mammals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dogs are vertebrates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some vertebrates are not mammals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All dogs are carnivores.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dogs might be vertebrates.

explanations.correct: If all mammals are vertebrates and dogs are mammals, then by transitivity, dogs must be vertebrates.
explanations.A: Reversal trap — the stimulus says all mammals are vertebrates, not all vertebrates are mammals.
explanations.C: While true in the world, the stimulus does not entail this; it only establishes that all mammals are vertebrates.
explanations.D: The stimulus says nothing about diet or carnivory.
explanations.E: Must-be-true, not could-be-true; 'might' indicates uncertainty where the inference is certain.

difficultyReason: Simple conditional with one clear application. The antecedent is satisfied, so the consequent must follow.
stimulus: If a book is published by a university press, then it has undergone peer review. The novel 'Meridian' was published by Oxford University Press.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All books undergo peer review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Novels published by university presses are always academic in nature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 'Meridian' has undergone peer review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any book that undergoes peer review is published by a university press.

choices.label: E
choices.text: 'Meridian' might have undergone peer review.

explanations.correct: Oxford University Press is a university press. The stimulus says all books published by university presses undergo peer review. Therefore, 'Meridian' must have undergone peer review.
explanations.A: Too broad — the stimulus limits the rule to university press publications only.
explanations.B: The stimulus does not claim all university-press novels are academic.
explanations.D: Reversal of the conditional — the stimulus says university press implies peer review, not the converse.
explanations.E: Must-be-true, not could-be-true; 'might' weakens a certain inference.

difficultyReason: Two factual statements about a specific event. Correct answer directly restates a claim from the stimulus.
stimulus: Last year, the hospital admitted fewer emergency patients than the previous year. Emergency admissions are the hospital's primary revenue source.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hospital's revenue decreased last year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emergency admissions account for some portion of the hospital's revenue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital's emergency department is less efficient than in previous years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fewer people required emergency care last year than the year before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The hospital will admit fewer emergency patients this year than last year.

explanations.correct: If emergency admissions are the primary revenue source, they must account for some portion (likely a substantial one) of the hospital's revenue. This is directly entailed by the stimulus.
explanations.A: Too strong — fewer patients does not necessarily mean less revenue (prices could have risen).
explanations.C: Efficiency is not mentioned in the stimulus.
explanations.D: This conflates the hospital's admission patterns with the population's need; the stimulus does not establish causation.
explanations.E: Predicts the future based on one year of data; the stimulus does not justify this extrapolation.

difficultyReason: Straightforward numerical fact with one necessary consequence. No inference beyond counting and comparison.
stimulus: The research team consists of five chemists, three biologists, and two physicists. Every member of the team holds a doctoral degree.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every chemist on the research team holds a doctoral degree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The team has more biologists than physicists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The research team has ten members in total.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All doctoral degree holders are members of this research team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Physicists are less qualified than chemists or biologists.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says every member of the team holds a doctoral degree. Chemists are members of the team, so every chemist must hold a doctoral degree.
explanations.B: True numerically (3 > 2) but this is stated in the stimulus, not inferred; the question asks for what 'must also be true,' implying a deduction beyond restatement. However, it is technically entailed. Still, A is more clearly a logical inference.
explanations.C: True numerically but again, a restatement rather than an inference.
explanations.D: Reversal trap — the stimulus says team members have doctorates, not that all doctorate holders are on this team.
explanations.E: Qualification level is not addressed in the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Simple contrapositive application. The stimulus forbids one property; the correct answer applies the logical contrapositive.
stimulus: No reptiles are warm-blooded. Snakes are reptiles.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All cold-blooded animals are reptiles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Snakes are not warm-blooded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some reptiles are cold-blooded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Warm-blooded animals are not snakes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If an animal is warm-blooded, it might not be a reptile.

explanations.correct: No reptiles are warm-blooded means reptiles are not warm-blooded. Snakes are reptiles, so snakes are not warm-blooded.
explanations.A: Reversal trap — the stimulus does not say all cold-blooded animals are reptiles.
explanations.C: While likely true, the stimulus does not affirm that some reptiles are cold-blooded; it only denies they are warm-blooded.
explanations.D: While logically equivalent to B, it is less direct and reverses the subject-predicate structure unnecessarily.
explanations.E: Weakening with 'might' — the inference is certain, not probabilistic.

difficultyReason: Three simple facts about a domain with one direct entailment. No hidden conditional or ambiguity.
stimulus: All sculptures displayed in the museum's main gallery were created by living artists. The marble piece 'Form and Void' is on display in the main gallery. Therefore, 'Form and Void' was created by a living artist.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The museum's main gallery contains only sculptures created by living artists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All sculptures created by living artists are displayed in the museum's main gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sculptor of 'Form and Void' is still alive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 'Form and Void' is made of marble.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Living artists create marble sculptures.

explanations.correct: The stimulus already contains a conclusion: 'Form and Void' was created by a living artist. Thus the sculptor is (or was at the time of creation) a living artist, meaning the sculptor is still alive (or was when the work was made—most naturally read as still alive).
explanations.A: Scope issue — the stimulus says all displayed works were created by living artists, not that the gallery contains only sculptures.
explanations.B: Reversal trap — the stimulus does not say all works by living artists are in the main gallery.
explanations.D: Restatement of the stimulus, not a new inference; the question implies deriving something beyond what is stated.
explanations.E: Too broad — the stimulus does not establish that all living artists create marble sculptures.

difficultyReason: Two statements about complementary properties. One clear negation entailment.
stimulus: All citizens are either registered voters or non-citizens. Chen is a citizen.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chen is a registered voter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chen is not a non-citizen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some registered voters are citizens.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If Chen is not a registered voter, then Chen is a non-citizen.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Non-citizens are never citizens.

explanations.correct: Chen is a citizen. The stimulus does not say all citizens are registered voters; it says citizens are either voters or non-citizens. But since Chen is a citizen, Chen cannot be a non-citizen, so Chen is not a non-citizen.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus allows citizens to be either registered voters OR non-citizens, not necessarily voters.
explanations.C: Likely true, but not entailed by the stimulus (we know only that Chen is a citizen, not whether Chen is a registered voter).
explanations.D: This logically follows but rephrases the original statement in a way that does not add new information. B is the cleaner inference.
explanations.E: Definition, not inference from the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Simple factual statement about a policy. Correct answer restates a direct entailment from the stimulus.
stimulus: All employees at the firm must complete annual ethics training. Rajesh is an employee at the firm.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rajesh has already completed ethics training this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ethics training is the most important professional development at the firm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rajesh must complete annual ethics training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Employees who do not complete ethics training are not employed at the firm.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Annual ethics training improves employee conduct.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes a universal rule: all employees must complete annual ethics training. Rajesh is an employee. Therefore, Rajesh must complete the training.
explanations.A: Conflates the requirement with its fulfillment; we know Rajesh must complete it, not that Rajesh has done so.
explanations.B: Value judgment not supported by the stimulus.
explanations.D: Contrapositive phrasing of the rule, logically equivalent to C but less direct.
explanations.E: Causal claim not supported by the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Two facts about overlapping sets. Correct answer uses set intersection logic.
stimulus: All organisms that photosynthesize contain chlorophyll. All plants contain chlorophyll. Some plants photosynthesize.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All plants photosynthesize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some organisms that photosynthesize are plants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chlorophyll is only found in plants.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organisms that do not photosynthesize do not contain chlorophyll.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All organisms that contain chlorophyll photosynthesize.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says some plants photosynthesize. Plants are organisms. Therefore, some organisms that photosynthesize are plants.
explanations.A: The stimulus says 'some plants photosynthesize,' not 'all plants photosynthesize.'
explanations.C: Overreach — the stimulus does not say chlorophyll is only in plants.
explanations.D: Contrapositive of the first statement leads to: if no chlorophyll, then does not photosynthesize. The stimulus does not entail this direction.
explanations.E: Reversal trap — the stimulus says photosynthesizers have chlorophyll, not that all organisms with chlorophyll photosynthesize.

difficultyReason: Single conditional fact with a negation. One straightforward contrapositive inference.
stimulus: Whenever a contract requires signature by a notary public, the contract is binding. The purchase agreement does not require a notary's signature.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The purchase agreement is not binding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The purchase agreement might not be binding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All binding contracts require a notary's signature.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contracts that do not require a notary's signature are not binding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is possible that the purchase agreement is binding for reasons other than notary signature.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says notary-signature is a sufficient condition for binding, not a necessary one. The purchase agreement lacks a notary signature, but this does not prevent it from being binding via other means.
explanations.A: Denying the antecedent fallacy — the stimulus does not say the only way a contract is binding is via notary signature.
explanations.B: Correct conclusion but uses 'might' (uncertainty) where 'must' or 'can' (possibility) is more appropriate.
explanations.C: Reversal trap — the stimulus says notary signature implies binding, not that binding implies notary signature.
explanations.D: Denying the antecedent — again, lack of notary signature does not entail lack of binding.
explanations.E: Correct — the stimulus permits (does not rule out) the purchase agreement being binding through other means.
